title: Dirt, mess and cleaning
summary: Mess in Supermarket Simulator is its own object: the game tracks dirt, shows how dirty something is, and gives cleaning its own state and animations.
body: Dirt is modelled rather than painted on, which is why the game can know how dirty something is instead of only showing you a stain.
Cleaning has its own state and its own animations, so mopping or washing a window is a task with a beginning and an end rather than a decoration.
Because dirtiness is measured, the shop's condition is something the game can react to without a customer telling you.
What this entry does not tell you: how quickly dirt appears, how much of it changes anything, or what customers do about it. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Dirt is its own object in the game.
How dirty something is can be indicated to the player.
Cleaning has a tracked state of its own.
Cleaning something has its own animation.
The build ships a dirt marker with a controller of its own, and a dust effect for cleaning.
facts.evidence: asset names: DirtIndicatorController, Dirt Indicator, Cleaning Dust

facts.claim: Dishwasher tablets are shipped as objects of their own among the shop's cleaning supplies.
facts.evidence: asset names: Dishwasher Tablet_Cemagik, Dishwasher Tablet_Boum

facts.claim: A third dishwasher tablet variant is shipped beside them.
Dirt marks are shipped as named sheets of their own, including one for spilt milk and one for the alien mess.
The build names a dirty rag of its own and an animation clip for a janitor cleaning up dirt.
facts.evidence: asset names: Rag_Dirty, Janitor Dirt Cleaning
